title: Affine finite coherent factorization of a perfect coefficient arrow
statement:
Let $D$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $D\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and let $S$ be a commutative finite type $D$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-scheme] and, for a commutative $D$-algebra $E$ with a specified map $E\to A$, put $Y_E=\operatorname{Spec}(S\otimes_D E)$ and let $\pi_E:Y_A\to Y_E$ be the projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. On $Y$, use $\mathcal B=\mathcal O_Y\otimes_D R_A$, $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal B)$, $U$, $\Phi_E$, $\widehat K$, perfection, and the action arrow $\nu_E$ of [def-sfb-dg-coefficient-realization]. Let $H$ be perfect over $\mathcal B$, let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{Y_A})$ [def-pc-derived-category], let $u:H\to\widehat K$ be a dg-derived morphism, and let $m\in\mathbf Z$. Assume $H^i(Uu)$ is surjective as a morphism of sheaves for every $i\ge m$.

There exist a finite type commutative $D$-algebra $E$ with $D\to E\to A$, an object $G\in D(\mathcal O_{Y_E})$ with bounded coherent cohomology [pqf-def-coherent], an ordinary scheme-derived morphism $\gamma:G\to R\pi_{E*}K$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image], and $\sigma:H\to\Phi_E(G)$ in $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal B)$, such that $\nu_E(\gamma)\circ\sigma=u$ and $H^i(U\sigma)$ is surjective for every $i\ge m$. The coefficient maps need not be flat; no injectivity of $H^i(Uu)$ or relative pseudo-coherence of $K$ is required.

proof.text: Use the affine dg comparison with $C_E=S\otimes_D R_E$ and $T_E=S\otimes_D E$. It sends $H$ to a perfect $P\in D(C_A)$, $K$ to an ordinary $T_A$-complex $L$, and $u$ to $v:P\to\operatorname{Res}_{C_A}^{T_A}L$. Cohomology is identified by associated sheaves, including the stated surjectivity hypotheses. The comparison gives an integer $b_H$ with $H^i(UH)=0$ for $i>b_H$.

source.place: Agent assembly of the affine descente subproblem following Tag 0CSD (lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general); the paragraph itself does not prove this assertion.

proof.text: Descend $P$ to a perfect $P_E$ over $C_E$, with $E$ finite type over $D$ and $C_A\otimes_{C_E}^{\mathbf L}P_E\simeq P$. By the dg scalar adjunction, $v$ has an adjoint $a:P_E\to\operatorname{Res}_{C_E}^{T_A}L$. Put $F=T_E\otimes_{C_E}^{\mathbf L}P_E$. Extension is exact and carries the regular module to $T_E$ and retracts to retracts; hence $F$ is perfect in the ordinary sense, by the perfectness compatibility in the affine comparison. If $s_1,\ldots,s_a$ and $e_1,\ldots,e_c$ generate $S$ and $E$ over $D$, then $s_j\otimes1$ and $1\otimes e_k$ generate $T_E$ over $D$. The finite-type Noetherianity theorem makes $T_E$ Noetherian. The affine equivalence sends $F$ to a perfect ordinary object $G$ on the Noetherian affine scheme $Y_E$; the perfect-cohomology theorem makes $G$ bounded coherent.

proof.text: The same adjunction along $C_E\to T_E$ transposes $a$ to $c:F\to\operatorname{Res}_{T_E}^{T_A}L$. Under the affine comparison this is an ordinary $\gamma:G\to R\pi_{E*}K$. Let $\eta:P_E\to\operatorname{Res}_{C_E}^{T_E}F$ be the unit and extend it to $C_A$. Using the descent isomorphism and the comparison with $\Phi_E$, this gives $s:H\to\Phi_E(G)$. The triangle identity says that extending $a$ and applying the $C_A$-action counit recovers $v$. Substituting $a=\operatorname{Res}(c)\eta$ gives $\nu_E(\gamma)s=u$, since the comparison identifies the actual action counit with $\nu_E$.

proof.text: The object $G$ is bounded above, say in degrees $\le b_G$. By the affine comparison, $\Phi_E(G)$ is the extension along $C_E\to C_A$ of the restriction of an ordinary $T_E$-module complex representing $G$, which may be truncated to vanish above $b_G$ (keeping its $T_E$-action), and $U$ is its underlying complex. The coefficient resolutions are nonpositive, so their relative bar extension of a representative zero above $b_G$ has no terms above $b_G$: each bar suspension lowers degree, and every algebra factor has nonpositive degree. Consequently $H^i(U\Phi_E(G))=0$ for $i>b_G$. Take $b=\max(m,b_H,b_G)$. The supplied factorization from step 3 is then surjective on underlying cohomology for every $i>b$, since its target is zero there.

proof.text: Induct down the finite list $b,b-1,\ldots,m$. At a stage $r$, retain a finite type coefficient algebra and a bounded coherent factorization with first map onto in degrees $i>r$. The one-degree refinement applies: $H^r(Uu)$ is onto because $r\ge m$. Its output extends the coefficient algebra and supplies a new factorization with first map onto for all $i\ge r$, which is precisely the hypothesis $i>r-1$ for the next stage. After $b-m+1$ applications obtain $E_f,G_f,\gamma_f,s_f$ onto in every degree $i\ge m$. At each extension adjoin its finite set of algebra generators to the generators already retained; a finite union of finite sets is finite, so $E_f$ is finite type over $D$. Every refinement retains the ordinary type of $\gamma_f$ and the actual equation $\nu_{E_f}(\gamma_f)s_f=u$. These data are the requested witnesses. For an empty $Y$, all objects are zero and the same conclusion follows by taking $E=D$ and $G=0$.
